I have been working this land for over five decades. Quzhou soil I know like my own hands — the sandy loam, the summer rains that come heavy and then stop, the dry springs that demand the well. My three mu of chili go in first, because that is where the money is. The rest of my land I run the old winter wheat and summer maize rotation I have done since I was a young man.

At my age I cannot do everything myself anymore. My wife and one other family member help, but heavy tillage I hire out. I am not going to start experimenting with new methods at 72. What has worked for 55 years will work again.

**Chili (4 mu):** This is my main income crop. I use the improved local variety from the county seed station — not the expensive hybrid, which I don't trust for this field's drainage. I fertilize heavily because chili takes it. I irrigate often during fruit set — the well is reliable. Pests and disease are my biggest worry, especially aphids and blight in July. I spray five times, maybe six if it's a wet summer.

**Winter wheat (6.1 mu):** I plough this field in October before sowing. I use the county-recommended improved variety. Four irrigations: at sowing, jointing, heading, and grain fill. I keep inputs moderate — wheat is not my cash crop, it feeds the household and covers costs.

**Summer maize (6.1 mu, same land as wheat):** After wheat harvest in June I go straight to hybrid seed and direct seeding — no tilling, saves my back and the soil moisture. I top-dress urea at topping stage. Two to three irrigations depending on July rains.
